keys.guide.anthropic:
1. Open platform.claude.com and create an account (or sign in).
2. Add credit under Billing (API use is paid separately from a chat subscription).
3. Settings → API keys → Create key; give it a name.
4. Copy the key (it is shown once) and paste it here.
5. Press "Save and test the connection".
keys.guide.openai:
1. Open platform.openai.com and sign in.
2. Add a payment method and credit under Billing.
3. API keys → Create new secret key.
4. Copy the key and paste it here.
5. Press "Save and test the connection".
keys.guide.openrouter:
1. Open openrouter.ai and sign in.
2. Buy credits (a small fee is added when buying).
3. Settings → Keys → Create key.
4. Copy the key and paste it here.
5. Press "Save and test the connection". OpenRouter reports the exact cost of every call.
keys.guide.zai:
1. Open z.ai and sign in.
2. Add balance to the API account.
3. API Keys → create a key.
4. Copy the key and paste it here.
5. Press "Save and test the connection".
keys.guide.mistral:
1. Open console.mistral.ai and sign in.
2. Choose a plan and add a payment method.
3. API Keys → Create new key.
4. Copy the key and paste it here.
5. Press "Save and test the connection".
keys.guide.deepseek:
1. Open platform.deepseek.com and sign in.
2. Top up the balance.
3. API keys → Create API key.
4. Copy the key and paste it here.
5. Press "Save and test the connection".
keys.guide.fal:
1. Open fal.ai and sign in.
2. Add credit under Billing.
3. Dashboard → Keys → Add key.
4. Copy the key and paste it here.
5. fal has no free test request: the key is checked when it is first used for an image or speech.

report.tooltip: Prepare the logs and open a GitHub issue. Nothing is sent automatically.
report.title: Report a problem
report.intro: Nothing is sent automatically. TM Concept has no telemetry: you decide what to share, and you attach it yourself.
report.contains:
“Prepare logs” makes a zip file in the data folder (reports) and shows it. It contains:
• the log files of the last 7 days. Before they go in, your home folder, the app's folders, e-mail addresses and keys are masked, and while the app is unlocked every profile name and concept or video title it knows becomes <name> (the activity lines of 0.1.4 leave them out already)
• system.txt: version, operating system, architecture, .NET, interface language, drawing mode and which tools are installed
It never contains your database, API keys, concept or narration texts, or video files. The logs do say which settings you changed and to what (interface language, drawing mode, notifications, each step's model, effort and engine). Masking is a safety net, not a guarantee: open the zip and read it before you share it publicly.
report.steps: “Report on GitHub” opens the issue form in your browser with the version and the system filled in: describe what happened and drag the zip into the form (a GitHub account is needed). “Copy details” copies the system information to the clipboard.
